raised.claim: Verdicts attached to newly proposed issues are never checked against the proposed issue's scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a proposal has scope `candidates_count > 0` but its referenced row has `candidates_count = 0`, the key is allowed and the verdict is still added to the new issue, so the job creates an issue carrying evidence that directly contradicts its rendered scope.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not account for other attachments planned for the same issue in the current run.
raised.why_it_breaks: When an issue has 11 post-creation rows and the current analysis routes two new rows to it, both verdicts see the unchanged value 11 and are accepted, leaving the issue with 13 rows despite the configured maximum of 12.

raised.claim: Any nonempty `beer_ids` list makes a scope legal even when its `where` clause still declares an entire review class.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope such as `{beer_ids:[1], where:[{col:'review_class',op:'=',value:'matcher_bug'}]}` passes legality; because IDs and `where` are alternatives in `rowSatisfiesScope`, every future matcher_bug row satisfies the class predicate, recreating the whole-class dumping ground the guard is intended to reject.

raised.claim: The absence guard treats one empty probe as proof even if the other probe returned hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a probe like `{brewery: '', name: 'Matching Beer'}`, `proved` is true due to the empty brewery result, so a `not_on_untappd` verdict survives even though the name probe found results; this contradicts the stated rule that a probe returning hits is not absence evidence.

raised.claim: Guard counters are not logged when every batch row received a model verdict, even if guards rejected those verdicts.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model returns one verdict for every orphan but all attachments violate scope, `covered` still equals `orphans.length`, so this warning is skipped and the nonzero `scope_violation` counter is never surfaced despite all rows remaining untriaged.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: Model-authored issue prose can place a valid `triage-scope` block before the trusted block and hijack parsing on the next run.
raised.why_it_breaks: If `issue.body` contains a valid fenced `triage-scope` block, the job appends its trusted block afterward, while `parseScopeBlock` uses the first regex match; the next run therefore enforces the model-authored scope rather than the structured scope that was validated and rendered by the job.

raised.claim: The tool schema accepts arbitrary columns, operators, and incompatible value types that the Zod scope schema rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: The model can validly submit tool output such as `{col:'candidate_count',op:'greater_than',value:0}` under this JSON schema, but `AnalysisSchema` rejects it because `ScopeTermSchema` uses constrained enums, causing the whole triage analysis to fail instead of strict tool use preventing the invalid output.

raised.claim: Quiet `matcher_bug` verdicts introduced by the new degradation path are counted as `wontfix`.
raised.why_it_breaks: When an unsupported `not_on_untappd` verdict is degraded to `matcher_bug`, it is pushed into `plan.quiet`; this loop takes the `else` branch and increments `outcome.wontfix`, so the persisted digest falsely reports the row as wontfix.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Reopening a triaged row clears its review fields but leaves the newly authoritative `issue_number` link stale.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a row attached to issue 408 crosses from zero to nonzero candidates, this upsert sets its class, note, and reviewed timestamp to NULL but preserves `issue_number = 408`; queries treating the new column as the authoritative row-to-issue link will continue to report an attachment for an untriaged row.

raised.claim: The saturation count measures only currently retained/currently linked failure rows, not all rows historically attached after issue creation.
raised.why_it_breaks: When an attached failure later matches, `clearEnrichFailure` deletes it, and when a row is rerouted its single `issue_number` is overwritten; either event reduces this count, allowing an issue that has already accepted 12 or more post-creation attachments to fall below the threshold and accept additional rows.
